question_record.context: A security incident involving suspicious access to the LSASS service was recorded, where multiple public tools or custom ones could be used by attackers to obtain clear-text passwords from LSASS service's memory. This was followed by lateral movement activities involving PSExec to jump server and ransomware payload remotely launched on a device. The attackers might be attempting to encrypt content on the device, making it unusable to users. The next alert triggered was due to a suspicious WMI process creation, potentially used by malware to spawn new processes and further infect the machine.
question_record.question: Can you identify the AadUserId related to the suspicious WMI process creation event?
solution: There was a suspicious access to the LSASS service by the user with SID `S-5-7-21-1843151660-3234030288-105586167-1422`.
A ransomware payload was remotely launched by the user with AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96`.
Suspicious WMI process creation was observed on the machine and was linked to the user with AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96`.
Lateral movement to the jump server was performed using PSExec by an IP address `99.83.111.100`.

15.name: Suspicious access to LSASS service
15.description: In order to obtain clear-text password, attackers must decrypt the user's password from the LSASS service's memory. Multiple public tools as well as custom ones could be used to perform this operation. Once obtained, these credentials are often used in lateral movement activities to infiltrate other machines and servers in the network.

174.name: PSExec to Vnevado-jump
174.description: Lateral movement to the jump server

112.name: Ransomware payload remotely launched.
112.description: A ransomware payload was remotely launched on this device. Attackers might be attempting to encrypt content on this device, rendering it unusable to users. For more information, read the Threat Analytics report, Threat overview: Human-operated ransomware: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/05658b6c-dc62-496d-ad3c-c6a795a33c27/analystreport

117.name: Suspicious WMI process creation
117.description: Suspicious WMI process creation was observed on the machine. Malware frequently use WMI to spawn new processes, breaking process trees and further infecting a machine.
